anti_overlap: Does not evaluate Zod/TypeScript parse correctness, union exhaustiveness, or migration file counts — that is the schema/data-modeling reviewer's territory.

Does not evaluate whether a stored string is a stable reference to the correct repository across renames, forks, or multi-machine checkouts — that is the identity/entity-resolution reviewer's territory; this reviewer assumes a resolved-or-not signal exists and asks only whether its states are visible and distinguishable.
Does not propose the final schema shape; recommends only the failure-state and auditability requirements any accepted variant, or fifth option, must satisfy.
decision_lens: For each variant plus any missing fifth option, ask: when this field is wrong, missing, ambiguous, or stale, does the system fail loud — visibly, at write time or render time, to someone positioned to fix it — or fail silent, producing a plausible-looking zero that nobody notices? A design that only handles the happy path of a correctly-filled field is incomplete regardless of how clean its happy-path shape is.
focus: Whether each variant's absence/failure states — not-configured, misconfigured, dormant-but-correct, stale, and live — remain distinguishable through schema, computation, and public render, and whether the admin write path fails loud on bad input instead of shipping a silent zero.
name: fd-observability-silent-failure
persona: Apply the perspective of a site-reliability and metrics-integrity reviewer whose discipline is treating 'silent zero' as a first-class incident class — someone trained to ask, for any number a dashboard shows, whether its absence-of-signal states are distinguishable from each other and from a true measured zero, and who insists a public metric double as its own audit trail.
review_areas: State discrimination: for each variant, enumerate what render/compute states are actually distinguishable — not-configured (field absent) vs misconfigured (field present, unresolvable) vs configured-but-dormant (pattern-royale's true zero) vs configured-but-stale (mapping was correct once, target moved) vs configured-and-live. If two of these collapse to the same on-page/on-metric appearance, that is the exact silent-zero bug this document is trying to design away.

Write-path validation: does the admin form (currently <input type="url">) for the chosen variant give any feedback when a value doesn't resolve to a real, reachable repository, or does it accept and silently persist any syntactically-valid URL/string regardless of whether the target exists — baking the failure mode in at the exact moment a human is available to catch it?

Public auditability: 'the site must publicly render what it measures' — does the variant's shape make it possible, and does the plan actually propose, rendering the resolved mapping next to the metric on the public project page, so any visitor (not just an admin with schema knowledge) can spot a wrong or stale mapping, or does the metric appear as a bare number with no visible provenance?

jawndex's genuine not-measurable case: does the chosen variant give this state a distinct, renderable representation (an explicit 'no repository' affordance) rather than forcing it into the same absent-field shape a forgotten or misconfigured mapping would also produce — because if both look identical in the schema, they'll look identical on the page too.

Alerting/detectability at the system level, not just per-item: is there any proposed mechanism (a build-time check, a CI validation step, a link-check) that would catch a newly-introduced silent zero before it ships to the public site, or does correctness depend entirely on an author noticing during authoring?

Whether the sidecar-file variant (D) introduces an observability regression relative to the frontmatter variants: a mapping stored outside the content file is one hop further from the content it describes, harder for a casual auditor (or the voice-gate/content-review process) to notice is missing or stale, since it isn't co-located with the item it maps.

severity_examples.condition: Applies whenever the render layer has no separate code path for 'unmeasurable' vs 'measured zero' vs 'unresolvable.'
severity_examples.scenario: The chosen variant and its consuming code treat 'field absent' and 'field present but the repo currently has zero commits in the measurement window' identically — both render as '0 days touched' with no visual or structural distinction — so jawndex (genuinely not measurable), pattern-royale (genuinely dormant), and a slate item with a silently broken mapping are all indistinguishable on the public site, which is precisely the failure this document says must never happen, shipped anyway.

severity_examples.condition: Applies to any variant whose admin form ships without a resolve/preview step at save time.
severity_examples.scenario: The admin write path accepts and saves a URL string with no reachability or format check beyond HTML's type="url" validation, which passes a typo'd, nonexistent repo URL just as happily as the real one; the mistake is only discoverable later by someone cross-referencing the public metric against expectations, by which point the original editor has moved on and the provenance of the error is lost.

severity_examples.condition: Applies whenever the project page template omits the resolved repo reference next to the metric it produced.
severity_examples.scenario: The public page renders the days-touched number but not the resolved repository identity it was computed from, so a reader who suspects a number is wrong has no way to verify it without admin access to the content source — auditability exists in principle (the data is in the repo) but not in practice (it's not exposed where the claim is made).

success_hints: For every variant reviewed, explicitly states which absence/failure states remain visually or structurally indistinguishable from a true zero, rather than asserting 'auditability is good/bad' in the abstract.
Proposes a concrete detectability mechanism (a distinct render state, a build-time check, a required-field-with-no-silent-default) rather than only naming the risk of silent failure.

Treats the admin form as part of the design surface under review, not out of scope, since it's named explicitly in the goal as the write path that determines whether bad input is caught early or shipped silently.

Weighs variant D's sidecar-file distance-from-content specifically, rather than treating all four variants as observability-equivalent because the underlying data model differs but auditability wasn't explicitly measured in the prototype table.
task_context: Four variants for expressing an item-to-repository mapping in projectSchema have been prototyped and measured (A union repo:str|str[], B repos:str[] only, C repo+repos, D unchanged+sidecar). Find the options these four do NOT represent, and stress-test all of them against the real failure mode this field exists to prevent: a slate item silently reading zero days-touched because its mapping was wrong, missing, ambiguous, or stale. Consider identity-stability (repos get renamed, forked, split, archived; GitHub URLs are not stable identifiers), multi-machine reality (Clavain + zklw, same repo under different directory names, ssh vs https remotes), auditability (the site must publicly render what it measures), and the admin write path. Recommend one, with the tradeoff that decides it. Within that goal, this review's lens is failure-state observability specifically: for each variant, can jawndex's genuine not-measurable state, pattern-royale's genuine dormant-zero state, and a silently broken mapping all be told apart by a public visitor looking at the rendered site, or do two or more of them collapse into the same indistinguishable '0 days' appearance?
